title: Crystal Dynamics has another round of layoffs, the sixth round since 2020, when they shipped their last game Marvel Aven
title_en:
Crystal Dynamics has another round of layoffs, the sixth round since 2020, when they shipped their last game Marvel Avengers🚀

✅Developers like UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, and senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker sharing news of their job cuts on LinkedIn.

✅Three sets of cuts in 2025 alone following financial upheaval at parent company Embracer Group and the cancellation of Perfect Dark.

✅Laid-off artist Kevin Baker had integrated tools like Claude Code and procedural tech for upcoming projects like Tomb Raider: Catalyst, highlighting the studio's use of generative AI despite ongoing staff reductions.

✅Despite the continuous reduction in workforce, and previous broken assurances from Embracer Group that the studio would be unaffected, 

Crystal Dynamics maintains that it remains fully committed to their upcoming Tomb Raider games.

Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is set to arrive February 12, 2027 and Catalyst would come after, but has been delayed after initially planning Legacy of Atlantis for 2026 and Catalyst for 2027.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 针对GPT-6.2 Astra模型的实测反馈显示，该模型在执行长周期复杂任务时表现出严重的逻辑冗余与任务递归，且无法精准识别自身知识库的局限性。使用者指出其输出结构解析难度高，在面对多环节交互时极易陷入无限循环。

elements_zh.what: 缺乏知识盲区感知，长任务逻辑递归与解析困难
elements_zh.why: 模型对复杂指令的上下文管理与规划能力尚未达到稳定工业级水准

elements_en.what: Lack of knowledge gap awareness, logical recursion, and parsing difficulties
elements_en.why: Deficiencies in long-context management and strategic reasoning

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 当前大模型在处理超长指令流时，‘注意力分配失焦’与‘思维链偏离’仍是技术瓶颈，单纯扩增上下文窗口并不能解决逻辑推理的有效性。该现象反映出模型在复杂任务规划（Agentic Planning）层面的架构冗余，未实现真正的任务解耦与自我博弈验证。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The current performance deficiency highlights that simply expanding the context window fails to solve reasoning drift and focus loss in complex task flows. title_en:
I've been talking to a bunch of PhD students and researchers recently, and I've qualitatively noticed two growing (but concerning) trends with AI:

1. Researchers seem to be reading less. Some even reported that they read <10 papers a year now with AI because they can simply either 1) retrieve or 2) summarize papers. BUT deep reading is how we engage with underlying intellectual arguments, develop research taste, spot methodological flaws, and form original ideas. It's arguably the most fun part of a PhD imo

2. Researchers seem to be vibe-coding and paper-maxxing. AI dramatically cheapens execution, such as implementing experiments, running analyses, and producing manuscripts. Some even "let [Claude Code] rip" without checking the code or validating the results somehow. BUT it also incentivizes quantity over depth, rigor, and meaningful contributions.

Overall, the cost of producing research is falling much faster than the cost of developing genuine intellectual understanding. Rather than simply producing more papers, I think we should engage deeply with the literature, ask questions that truly matter, and produce work that meaningfully advances our collective understanding.

full_text_zh:
最近，我一直在与一群博士生和研究人员交谈，我定性地注意到人工智能的两个不断增长（但令人担忧）的趋势：

1. 研究人员的阅读量似乎减少了。有些人甚至报告说，他们现在使用人工智能每年阅读不到 10 篇论文，因为他们可以简单地 1) 检索或 2) 总结论文。但深度阅读是我们参与潜在知识论点、培养研究品味、发现方法论缺陷和形成原创想法的方式。在我看来，这可以说是博士学位中最有趣的部分

2. 研究人员似乎在进行振动编码和论文最大化。人工智能极大地降低了执行成本，例如实施实验、运行分析和制作手稿。有些人甚至“让[Claude Code]撕裂”而不检查代码或以某种方式验证结果。但它也鼓励数量而非深度、严谨性和有意义的贡献。

title: ‼️ A hacked laptop can pass its "trusted device" status in Cisco, Palo Alto, Zscaler and Netskope VPNs to the attacker's
title_en:
‼️ A hacked laptop can pass its "trusted device" status in Cisco, Palo Alto, Zscaler and Netskope VPNs to the attacker's own machine. Researcher Ruslan Sayfiev showed it at Tokyo's CODE BLUE conference.

He used copied sessions, exported certificates and faked device health checks. TPM security chips only stop the keys being copied, not used, he said.

GMO Flatt Security, a Japanese security firm, scanned 19.2M open-source packages over 181 days. Malicious ones were published every single day, 31,840 in all.

It traced October's hijack of LiteLLM, an AI tool with about 100M monthly downloads, to an admin key that leaked in May and was never revoked.

A state-backed Iranian group has spied on protest supporters since January with fake frontline reports, stealing browser logins, Telegram data and keystrokes.

And opening a cloned repo in Claude Code, Cursor or Gemini CLI can run an attacker's code before you approve anything.

Engineers are finishing the patch. We’re asking our workforce to stay patient, stay off Signal and stagger their arrivals until further notice.

To everyone outside the agency: your communications were never interrupted. We’d know.

我从未感到如此多的被看见。我们很大。我们很强大。国会刚刚向情报界拨款 781 亿美元。类似的事情时有发生。没关系。

人们会询问领导力。我对此表示欢迎。 2025 年 4 月，我们的主任蒂莫西·豪 (Timothy Haugh) 将军在活动人士劳拉·卢默 (Laura Loomer) 会见总统后被解雇。 2026 年 3 月，参议院以 71 比 29 的投票结果确认了他的继任者约书亚·拉德将军。拉德将军是一名职业特种作战军官。 Breaking Defense 报道称，他来找我们时“在信号情报和网络世界上几乎没有直接经验”。

参议员罗恩·怀登表示反对。他写道：“根本没有时间在职学习。”我谨表示不同意。周二是在职学习，整个机构都参加了。

钱不是问题。国会今年为国家情报计划拨款 781 亿美元，比去年增加了近 50 亿美元。我们要求 819 亿美元。我并不是说缺失的 38 亿美元是用于路由器的。我是说没有人能证明事实并非如此。

2025 年，我们有 349,823 个第 702 条目标。我们可以找到 349,823 名外国人。周二早上，我们无法给隔壁办公桌的分析师发消息。

白宫已要求参议院在 12 月 9 日之前重新授权第 702 条。如果国会想与我们讨论此事，请使用电话。我们的一直在工作。

我想向我们的员工致辞，无论他们身在何处、何时抵达。您今天可能想知道如何传达机密信息。请不要使用信号。 2025 年 2 月，我们发送了一份“运营安全特别公告”，警告我们的员工有关 Signal 的漏洞。下个月，国家安全高级官员使用 Signal 讨论军事打击计划，并在聊天中添加了一名记者。我们对我们的指导从未如此有信心。

有一个技术细节。该公告称，像 Signal 这样的应用程序“受到政策允许，可用于非保密问责/召回活动”。错峰抵达是一项问责制。因此，周二，Signal 可能在机构历史上首次符合政策。请不要推动它。

请稍后再试。

title: SGLang Summit wrapped with NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Meta, Thinking Machines Lab, Intel, Cloudflare, Modal and RadixArk joini
title_en:
SGLang Summit wrapped with NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Meta, Thinking Machines Lab, Intel, Cloudflare, Modal and RadixArk joining the new SGLang Consortium to help shape the open-source inference roadmap.

Same day brought the announcement of SGLang v1.0 (built for production scale with better throughput, memory use and flexible scaling), SGLang running on AWS Trainium, a RadixArk–Intel partnership to optimize for Intel CPUs/GPUs/accelerators (improvements contributed back), and Miles v0.2 with broader hardware support.

Chip vendors that usually compete rarely back the same open project this explicitly. Fast, affordable inference is the practical constraint once models get larger and agents take on more real work - open foundations that multiple hardware vendors commit to are what make that scale accessible beyond a few closed stacks.

With linked billing, customers approve a link to the platform instead, so there are no customer API keys to share or store.

title_en:
devin bots are multi-agent teams done right:
- always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI)

- manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself)
- available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction)

this is the preview that @walden_yan gave at AIE. i've been trialing them for a week and i've been able to hand over my AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin automation, and video editing work (also simultaneously moving from local agent worktree hell to cloud because ofc this is all cloud based thank god)

hyped concepts this replaces:
- /goal
- "ultracode" / "ultra mode"
- "loop engineering"
- "agent to agent"
- "agent swarms"
- AI employees (see below)

my main aha moment is that you don't want "AI Employees", we do not have agi yet and you will just fail if you overpromise/overexpect. what you want is the "just" the next level of abstraction above single tasks, and the overwhelming consensus I've had talking to everyone at the frontier of agents (yes incl cog competitors) is agent managers that own outcomes. 

incidentally, as an employer of humans it's also how i distinguish between someone who "has agency" (owns a problem area, finds issues and researches/brings solutions not problems) and who doesn't (only does precisely what i asked, not proactive, doesn't come up with suggestions i didn't think about). guess which one i value more lol.

title_en:
This is WILD

NVIDIA, AMD and Intel just signed on to the same open source project

These companies fight over every chip sale on the planet. They almost never back the same thing

But at SGLang Summit last week all three joined the new SGLang Consortium. Alongside Google, Meta, Thinking Machines Lab, Cloudflare, Modal and RadixArk

SGLang is the open source engine that runs AI models fast and cheap in production

Why would rivals team up? Simple:

Models are getting bigger. Agents are taking on more work. The model isn't the bottleneck anymore. Running it fast and affordably is

Nobody wins if every chip needs its own engine. So they're all building on one open one

Means a few things for you:

1. The software running your AI won't be locked to one chip company

2. Intel is now optimizing SGLang for its chips, and it just landed on AWS Trainium too. More hardware options, more competition on price

3. Open source isn't just for experiments anymore. Cloudflare, LinkedIn and HeyGen were there talking about running it for real users at scale

At the infrastructure layer the open vs closed debate is over

title_en:
One thing I find important when discussing AI-powered trading is knowing who actually controls the money when an agent starts making decisions.

Automation can save time, but giving an AI agent unrestricted access to funds creates a different kind of risk.

That's where @meetmotes, powered by @0xhazels, takes an interesting approach.

Instead of combining ownership, fund custody and transaction execution under one system, it separates these responsibilities.

Here's how I understand the model:

* Genesis NFT: Establishes ownership and acts as the holder's credential.

* Smart Account: Keeps the user's USDC under self-custody.

* AI Agent: Analyzes opportunities and proposes transactions without directly controlling the funds.

The most important part is the permission layer. The agent must operate within the rules the owner has approved and signed on-chain. Automation doesn't mean unlimited authority.

I think this distinction matters because the future of AI trading shouldn't be measured only by how many tasks an agent can perform. We should also consider what happens when it makes a bad decision or tries to go beyond its intended permissions.

For me, intelligent automation is valuable, but control over personal assets should never become an afterthought.

What's your priority in an AI trading system: more automation or stronger, independently verifiable control over your funds?

自动化可以节省时间，但让人工智能代理不受限制地访问资金会产生另一种风险。

这就是 @meetmotes（由 @0xhazels 提供支持）采取了一种有趣的方法。

它不是将所有权、资金托管和交易执行合并在一个系统下，而是将这些职责分开。

我是这样理解这个模型的：

* Genesis NFT：建立所有权并充当持有者的凭证。

* 智能账户：自行保管用户的USDC。

* AI代理：分析机会并提出交易，无需直接控制资金。

最重要的部分是权限层。代理人必须按照所有者在链上批准并签署的规则进行操作。自动化并不意味着无限的权力。

我认为这种区别很重要，因为人工智能交易的未来不应仅通过代理可以执行多少任务来衡量。我们还应该考虑当它做出错误决定或试图超出其预期权限时会发生什么。

对我来说，智能自动化很有价值，但对个人资产的控制永远不应该成为事后的想法。

您在人工智能交易系统中的首要任务是什么：更高的自动化程度还是对资金的更强大、可独立验证的控制？

title_en:
After nearly a year in stealth, I’m excited to be launching Stello.

Following Morning Brew’s acquisition of Our Future, I spent the last few years helping leading companies build what we now call New Media. My mission is no different from Stello’s today: help large enterprises adapt to a huge shift. 

Across the economy, established businesses operate at enormous scale, with decades of accumulated systems, processes and complexity. AI offers the opportunity to reimagine how these businesses operate, yet putting it into practice is far from straightforward.

While AI was built in San Francisco, its greatest returns will accrue to companies of all kinds. My co-founder Anan and I bonded over this shared conviction, so much so that we left Meta and Morning Brew to focus on it. 

We were most struck by the gap between AI’s potential and its adoption. 95% of enterprise AI pilots fail to deliver measurable ROI. The reality is that all organizations will need to be AI-first but the diffusion has barely begun. 

Implementing AI requires companies to fundamentally rethink established workflows. No two businesses operate the same way and so solutions need to be bespoke and deeply embedded in how businesses operate. 

Stello is the AI transformation company for the modern enterprise. We work as an extension of existing teams, combining their industry expertise with our technical capabilities to identify opportunities, build tailored AI solutions and drive adoption.

Over the last year, we’ve worked with 30+ enterprises across healthcare, financial services, insurance, retail and even professional sports. We’ve built an eight-figure pipeline without spending a dollar on marketing, all while staying fully bootstrapped.

The enduring value of AI will take far longer than a decade to diffuse across American companies. Realizing that potential requires exceptional technical talent alongside commercially minded operators who understand how businesses work.

We’re looking for ambitious, proactive people who want to take ownership from day one, work directly with clients on meaningful projects and see their work deployed at scale. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

And whether your company is just getting started with AI or knows exactly what it wants to build, let’s get in touch. We’ll help you get there.

full_text_zh:
经过近一年的默默无闻，我很高兴能够推出 Stello。

在 Morning Brew 收购 Our Future 后，我在过去的几年里帮助领先的公司建立我们现在所说的新媒体。我的使命与 Stello 今天的使命没有什么不同：帮助大型企业适应巨大的转变。

在整个经济中，成熟的企业规模庞大，拥有数十年积累的系统、流程和复杂性。人工智能提供了重新构想这些企业运作方式的机会，但将其付诸实践却远非易事。

虽然人工智能是在旧金山建立的，但其最大的回报将惠及各类公司。我和我的联合创始人 Anan 因这个共同的信念而紧密相连，以至于我们离开 Meta 和 Morning Brew 来专注于它。

人工智能的潜力与其应用之间的差距给我们留下了最深刻的印象。 95% 的企业人工智能试点未能提供可衡量的投资回报率。现实情况是，所有组织都需要以人工智能为先，但这种传播才刚刚开始。

实施人工智能需要公司从根本上重新思考既定的工作流程。没有两家企业的运营方式相同，因此解决方案需要定制并深深嵌入企业的运营方式中。

Stello 是现代企业的人工智能转型公司。我们作为现有团队的延伸，将他们的行业专业知识与我们的技术能力相结合，以发现机会、构建定制的人工智能解决方案并推动采用。

去年，我们与医疗保健、金融服务、保险、零售甚至职业体育领域的 30 多家企业合作。我们没有在营销上花费一美元就建立了一个八位数的管道，同时保持完全自力更生。

人工智能的持久价值需要十年以上的时间才能在美国公司中传播。实现这一潜力需要卓越的技术人才以及具有商业头脑且了解企业运作方式的运营商。

我们正在寻找雄心勃勃、积极主动的人才，他们希望从第一天起就拥有主动权，直接与客户合作开展有意义的项目，并看到他们的工作得到大规模部署。如果这听起来像您，我们很乐意听取您的意见。

无论您的公司刚刚开始使用人工智能，还是确切地知道自己想要构建什么，请与我们联系。我们将帮助您实现这一目标。
